title: Dynamic regional SKU commitment experiment plan
summary: Interactive experiment plan to test dynamic regional commitment thresholds for GPU SKUs. Goal: reduce overcommit and regional stockouts by treating commit decisions as experiments rather than fixed rules.
content:
Purpose:
Run a set of controlled experiments to determine whether dynamic, region-weighted SKU commitments (vs. static commit percentages) reduce total spend while keeping <48h cold-start probability <2% and median p95 latency impact <5ms.

Why this is different:
- Past decks assume global commit percentages and deterministic reorder points by SKU.
- This sheet treats commit sizing as an adaptive policy with A/B candidate thresholds by region tied to observed utilization and lead-time tails.

Primary metrics (to track daily):
- regional_utilization_p95 (percent)
- cold_start_probability_48h (percent)
- procurement_cost_usd_per_week
- unserved_capacity_minutes_per_week
- average_lead_time_days_by_sku

Assumptions (baseline for calculations):
- Payload: production inference 24/7.
- Unit: 1 slot = 1 GPU of SKU (normalized to H100-80GB equivalent for burn calculations).
- Demand smoothing window: 14d EWMA.
- Safety stock target: protects against 95th percentile lead time.

Key SKUs considered (example rows):
SKU, nominal_daily_slots, avg_lead_time_days, lead_time_p95_days, regional_fulfillment_preference
H100-80GB, 450, 42, 72, west-us > east-us > eu-west
A100-40GB, 250, 30, 55, eu-west > east-us > apac
L40S, 120, 21, 35, apac > east-us > eu-west
A30, 80, 18, 30, east-us > apac
T4-refurb, 40, 10, 22, fallback-only

Reorder point (baseline formula):
ROP = daily_demand * lead_time_mean + safety_stock
Where safety_stock = z * sqrt(lead_time_variance * daily_demand_variance + daily_demand_mean^2 * lead_time_variance)
(For experiments we simplify to safety_stock ~= 1.65 * observed_stdev_14d * sqrt(lead_time_mean)).

Experiment design (3-arm regional randomized):
- Control (static commit): current commit rule by SKU: global_commit_pct (H100 60%, A100 50%, L40S 40%). Orders placed when global ROP hit.
- Arm A (region-weighted static thresholds): precomputed per-region commit% proportional to 14d demand share; fixed for 8 weeks.
- Arm B (adaptive commitments): commit windows tuned daily by model: if regional_utilization_p95 > 85% AND cold_start_prob_48h > 1%, increase commit by 5% (capped), if utilization_p95 < 60% for 7d, decrease commit by 5%.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 0 (pilot): run Arm B in one small region (apac-sg) for H100 and L40S only; monitor supplier acceptance and lead time shifts.
2) Week 2: expand Arm A to eu-west for A100 only.
3) Week 4: run full 3-arm split across west-us / eu-west / apac-sg using traffic-routed buckets (simulated orders).
4) Week 8: evaluate 8-week delta on metrics and decide new baseline.

Sample calculations (H100, west-us):
- observed_daily_slots = 85
- mean_lead_time = 42 days
- lead_time_p95 = 72 days
- stdev_14d_daily_slots = 12
- approximate_safety_stock = 1.65 * 12 * sqrt(42) ≈ 1.65*12*6.48 ≈ 128 slots
- ROP ≈ 85 * 42 + 128 ≈ 3570 + 128 = 3698 slots => implies order cadence and lot size planning.
Notes: this highlights that for long lead-time SKUs, safety stock dominates and small reductions in lead time have outsized impact.

Order sizing heuristics for experiments:
- Minimum order lot = 16 GPUs (vendor MOQs)
- Prefer staggered 4-week slice orders to smooth arrival windows rather than single 12-week bulk when forecast uncertainty > 12%
- Leverage capability to convert a portion of orders to lease windows (spot/reserve) if supplier acceptance rate < 85% within 7d.

Risk & mitigation matrix (short):
- Supplier lead-time shift upward by >15%: trigger emergency rebalancing across regions and accelerate spot-lease buys; notify SRE and sales ops.
- Rapid demand spike (>30% 7d growth): tripwire to open burst leasing lane and short-term preemptible capacity.
- Vendor MOQ reduction request rejected: test partial acceptance with refurbishment program or staging orders via third-party brokers.

Data collection fields (columns for the sheet):
- date, region, sku, observed_daily_slots, demand_window_14d_mean, demand_14d_stdev, mean_lead_days, p95_lead_days, commit_pct, commit_policy_arm, order_placed_bool, order_size_slots, expected_arrival_date, actual_arrival_date, procurement_cost_usd, notes

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm vendor lead time distributions by vendor (we have only mean estimates for 3 vendors). Action: procurement to ask vendors for empirical delivery timelines (owner: Priya).
- Is there a constraint on inter-region transfer costs that would nullify micro-commit adjustments? Get finance to model cross-region transport costs per GPU (owner: Ethan).
- Test sensitivity to smaller safety_stock coefficient (1.2 vs 1.65) in a sandbox to quantify cost vs. cold-start risk.

Operational playbook snippet for procurement ops (for arm B dynamic behavior):
- Daily job synthesizes 14d EWMA demand per region per SKU.
- If model recommends commit change > 5% then throttle to 5% and create a manual review ticket for procurement.
- Weekends: aggregate changes; place orders only on Mon/Wed/Fri to batch vendor interactions.

Appendix: experiment variant examples (CSV slice):
variant,region,sku,baseline_commit_pct,armA_commit_pct,armB_init_commit_pct
control,west-us,H100,60,60,60
armA,eu-west,A100,50,45,50
armB,apac-sg,L40S,40,35,42

Decision criteria for productioning any policy: must beat control on at least two of: total procurement_cost_usd_per_week (lower by >=5%), cold_start_probability_48h (<= control), and regional_utilization_p95 (<= control + 3 percentage points).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally pragmatic (sheet first) so procurement and SRE can iterate quickly.
- If approved, I'll run a small backtest using historical order arrivals and demand from 2024 and produce a simulation report (expected by Week 3).

History / changes:
- 2025-01-12: created initial experiment plan (Michael).
- 2025-01-28: added rollout timeline and sample calculations (Sofia).
- 2025-02-20: revised risk matrix and tightened decision criteria (Ethan).

Action items (owner -> due):
- Priya: request vendor lead-time CSVs (due 2025-02-27).
- Ethan: run transport-cost model (due 2025-03-04).
- Michael: implement daily EWMA job prototype and baseline backtest (due 2025-03-07).

End of sheet.
